source.title: Ulster Herald, 21 September 1946, p. 5 ("Tyrone-Fermanagh bodies divided: L.C. elections")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: the members of the new Rural Council read in the Ulster Herald of 21 September 1946, p. 5.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. There were no contests: the 39 divisions were divided between 21 Unionists and the Nationalists, with a number of changes of person. Returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Mountjoy West' to Mountjoy Forest West (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): Mountjoy East and Mountjoy West are the short form of the DEDs Mountjoy Forest East and Mountjoy Forest West of Omagh Rural District (the 1911 DED map, 'Mountjoy Forest, East' and 'Mountjoy Forest, West'; the NI DED maps of 1925-39); the DED named Mountjoy alone lies in Dungannon Rural District. No round files both forms of one side, and the same members sit under both: John Johnston (Forest East 1924, 1927, 1933; East 1930, 1936), John Given (Forest West 1924, 1927, 1933; West 1930, 1936), J. K. McCollum (East 1946; Forest East 1949, 1952), W. G. Henderson (West 1946; Forest West 1949; West 1955); the Ulster Herald of 22 April 1939, p. 5, prints the council's 'Mountjoy East' and 'Mountjoy Forest West' nominations side by side. This round was filed as 'Mountjoy West', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (mountjoy-west) answers with a redirect to this one.
